description: Update dependencies to resolve security vulnerabilities: upgrade Next.js 14.2.15→15.x (or latest 14.x patch) to fix 3 critical (RCE, auth bypass) + 8 high severity issues; update postcss 8.4.47→8.5.x (2 high: path traversal); update vitest 2.1.3→latest (2 critical: RCE, arbitrary file read); update zod 3.23.8→3.x latest (1 high: DoS). Also update eslint 8→9, recharts 2→3, and other outdated but non-vulnerable deps.
steps: 1. Update Next.js and related packages: npm install next@latest eslint-config-next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest @types/react@latest @types/react-dom@latest. Verify compatibility (Next 15 may require React 19; check if app code is compatible or stay on Next 14.x latest patch).
2. Update critical security fixes: npm install postcss@latest vitest@latest (check if latest vitest has breaking changes; may need to update test files).
3. Update Zod: npm install zod@latest. Check if major version bump (3.x→4.x) has breaking changes in schema definitions used across validations/.

4. Update other outdated dependencies: npm install recharts@latest eslint@latest prettier@latest lucide-react@latest papaparse@latest tsx@latest autoprefixer@latest tailwindcss@latest tailwind-merge@latest typescript@latest (check TypeScript 5.6→7.x compatibility).
5. Update Prisma: npm install prisma@latest @prisma/client@latest && npm run db:generate. Check if schema or query syntax needs updates.
6. Update bcryptjs: npm install bcryptjs@latest @types/bcryptjs@latest. Verify password hashing still works (cost factor unchanged).
7. After all updates, run npm audit to verify vulnerabilities are resolved. Address any remaining issues.
8. Check for breaking changes: review changelogs for Next.js, Zod, Vitest, TypeScript major version bumps. Update code as needed.
9. Update next.config.mjs if Next.js 15 requires config changes (e.g., new compiler options, changed security headers format).
10. Run npm run typecheck && npm run lint to catch any API changes from dependency updates.
acceptance_criteria: npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities (or only low/moderate non-exploitable issues)
All critical and high severity CVEs are resolved
Next.js updated to secure version (15.x or 14.x latest with all patches)
Dependencies up to date with no known security issues
Application still compiles and passes type checks after updates
verification: npm audit --json | ConvertFrom-Json | Select-Object -ExpandProperty metadata | Select-Object -ExpandProperty vulnerabilities — critical and high counts must be 0
findings: Current vulnerabilities: Next.js 14.2.15 has 3 critical (GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36 RCE on Windows, GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 RCE via AVIF, GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw RCE via SVG, GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw auth bypass) + 8 high severity DoS/SSRF issues. Postcss 8.4.47 has 2 high (GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q, GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 path traversal). Vitest 2.1.3 has 2 critical (GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq RCE, GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp arbitrary file read). Tinypool (via vitest) has 2 critical prototype pollution. Zod 3.23.8 has 1 high (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 DoS). Many transitive vulnerabilities via glob, picomatch, micromatch, chokidar in dev dependencies. npm outdated shows: next 14.2.15→16.4.6, vitest 2.1.3→5.1.1, zod 3.23.8→4.6.7, eslint 8.57.1→10.15.0, recharts 2.13.0→3.11.0, prisma 5.20.0→8.0.0-rc.34, typescript 5.6.3→7.0.2, react 18.3.1→19.3.1.
